newsitem.title: UK: UK shares close at record high as Dow gains.
newsitem.headline: UK shares close at record high as Dow gains.

text.p: ** FTSE 100 ends at new peak as Dow gains and clutch of
leading UK company results beat expectations.
** U.S. producer prices, UK retail data broadly in line.
** BTR shares rise after restructuring statement.
** BAe, RTZ, Legal & General advance after results.
UK stocks rose to a record closing high on Thursday as a clutch of results from leading UK companies beat expectations and the Dow made a firm start.
The FTSE 100 index closed up 27.0 points at 3,932.6, surpassing its previous peak of 3,918.7 set August 28.

Gains in British Aerospace, Legal & General and RTZ helped fuel the advance after well-received results and BTR rose on restructuring news. Broadly in-line inflation data in the UK and US helped buoy bonds and equities yet share volume remained low and some said the UK market may struggle to gain further.
"We have seen a lot of earnings which have been slightly higher than expected," said Scott Evans, strategist at UBS, "and economic data has been supportive too."
"But I think we're going to see a lot of nervousness coming back into the market as next Fed meeting starts to loom and people start to worry about an interest rate hike in the U.S."
Trading volume reached a modest 613.7 million by 1556 GMT and gainers in the FTSE 100 were in a seven-to-two majority.
"Volume has been very low as the market has beeing going up and that is always a poor base for a market rally," Evans said. "I don't see much upside from here."

Yet the Dow was up 19.61 points at 5,774.53 shortly after the London close and the U.S. long bond was also higher, taking comfort from figures showing a 0.1 percent decline in core producer prices in August.

The Fed next meets on rate policy on September 24 and some say it could tighten policy even before then to ward off inflation pressures, though today's U.S. figures further cooled concerns about the pace of growth in the United States.
In the UK too reports showed little imminent inflation danger, with retail prices up a monthly 0.5 percent in August -- just a shade above market expectations.
Gilts also rose with the long gilt future up 9/32 at 107-17/32.

"The encouraging thing is that the unwinding of the summer sales was not that aggressive, which would indicate that generally pricing pressures remain fairly competitive," said Deutsche Morgan Grenfell economist Ciaran Barr.
London shares edged higher through the morning after a string of largely upbeat results from over 40 companies, including seven from the FTSE 100.
RTZ, British Aerospace, Legal & General, Caradon, United News & Media all pushed higher after results.
British Aerospace leapt 37p to a record 10.49-1/2 and Legal & General was up 17p at 745-1/2, also a record.

RTZ leapt 31p to 961-1/2, boosted by comments from the mining group that it saw signs of rising metal prices. And BTR rose 9-1/2p to 275-1/2 as the industrial conglomerate announced long-awaited restructuring plans.

Unilever was another strong feature, up 32-1/2p at 13.75 stg after an upbeat series of presentations in the US on the firm's outlook, with chairman Niall Fitzgerald repeating the company's targe of double-digit earnings growth for 1996 and 1997.
Yet ICI fell 7p to 838-1/2p as BZW lowered profit forecasts.
Light fittings group TLG tumbled 62p to 108-1/2p after it warned market conditions had deteriorated.
Traders and strategists said market attention would now shift to Friday's U.S. consumer prices and retail sales figures.
-- David Holmes, London Newsroom +44 171 542 5106
